title: Assembler accepts parts with failed per-part CRC without any warning
description:
add_part() does not inspect part.crc32_verified. When yencoding::decode() produces a DecodedPart with crc32_verified=false due to a CRC mismatch (not merely an absent CRC field), the assembler silently writes the corrupt bytes into the buffer.

The DecodedBlock.crc32_verified flag is true only when a pcrc32= field was present AND matched. False covers both 'CRC absent' and 'CRC mismatch'. The assembler cannot distinguish these cases from the outside.

Impact: a single corrupted part with a pcrc32= mismatch can silently corrupt the assembled file. The whole-file CRC check in finish() will catch the resulting file corruption only if set_expected_crc32() was called — but that field is optional, and many encoders omit the whole-file CRC (they include only per-part pcrc32=).

Fix options:
1. Reject parts where crc32_verified is false (conservative — breaks 'no CRC' articles).
2. Add a separate 'crc_checked' flag to DecodedPart that distinguishes 'verified OK' / 'mismatch' / 'absent', and reject only 'mismatch'.
3. Document clearly in add_part() that parts with CRC mismatches will be silently accepted and the whole-file CRC is the only safety net.

Option 3 is the minimum; option 2 is the correct fix.
